items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Mr. Dorsey liked me and I liked Mr. Dorsey... I was the happiest man up there with Mr. Dorsey.

ctx.x: That's right, and Mr. Dorsey liked me and I liked Mr. Dorsey, he was the one who worked on the wagon, called the White Wing, when the horses -- White Wing would get this stuff off the street because in Washington at that time the streets was clean, clean as could be and Mr. Dorsey would come and White Wings, they had white coats on and they looked something -- had something looked like our garbage can now and put this in his wagon and I'd be up there with Mr. Dorsey and that stuff was smelling and it smelt like…

So now here is my first sadness. He come up in the draft and he had to leave, see, and I had another uncle, he married my aunt, he had to leave, but Mr. Dorsey had to leave but before Mr. Dorsey got his draft notice, I was sleeping -- I don't know if I was sleeping or not, three pigeons come in
